peircean_analysis.firstness: auth.log last recorded entry at 17:38; file inode mtime 23:47 (touched 6h later). VIM editor signature in file slack space. PID 2891 recorded at 17:30 < PID 2934 at 16:15 (physically impossible — PID sequence is monotonically increasing). NetFlow shows two SSH sessions at 23:41 and 23:47 from 10.0.0.15 NOT appearing in auth.log. Session 1: 2.1MB in 84s. Session 2: 64 bytes in 17s. Kernel audit log: pg_dump executed at 23:41:15 as auid=1001/uid=0 against rrhh_empleados.db (847 employees, salary + banking). No ITSM change ticket.
peircean_analysis.secondness: System logs cannot be edited with VIM — they are written by the kernel logging daemon. PID regression is physically impossible in a running Linux kernel. The six-hour gap between last log entry and inode mtime is the editing window. The NetFlow sessions at 23:41/23:47 exactly fill the auth.log gap. Session 1 duration/size is consistent with pg_dump of an HR database. Session 2 duration/size is consistent with running vim and saving a modified log file. The combination of missing PIDs + VIM signature + inode timing + NetFlow sessions = log fabrication to cover two SSH sessions.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: Sysadmin Carlos M. (10.0.0.15) conducted unauthorized pg_dump of the HR employee database at 23:41, then at 23:47 manually edited auth.log to delete both SSH sessions. The log editing used vim (root privileges required to write to syslog-owned file). The PID regression in the edited log is a fabrication artifact — the attacker did not maintain PID sequence consistency. Anti-forensics applied post-exfiltration to deny presence. This is MALICE: active exfiltration + deliberate log tampering to conceal.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H2: Sysadmin authorized maintenance. pg_dump could be a late-night backup. Log modification could be correcting a corrupt entry.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H2 FULLY REFUTED: (A) PID 2891 < PID 2934 is a physical impossibility — cannot occur in normal system operation, only in manually edited text. (B) VIM signature in slack space proves a text editor was used on a system log — never legitimate. (C) No ITSM change ticket means no authorized maintenance window. (D) NetFlow records two sessions that auth.log has deliberately erased. Four independent contradictions refute H2.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H2 REFUTED. MALICE confirmed. original_verdict agrees.

devil_advocate: Carlos M. could have been performing emergency authorized maintenance without creating an ITSM ticket (happens in genuine emergencies). The pg_dump could be a legitimate backup to a new destination. However: the PID regression proves manual log editing — no legitimate maintenance requires tampering with process ID sequences in system logs. The VIM signature clinches it.
